scope: Final AbacusSummit cut-sky covariance and pair-window calibration for the five-tracer luminosity-proxy DESI DR1 odd-sector estimator.

covariance_interpretation.reason: The ensemble contains 25 mocks for an 18-dimensional vector. OAS regularization improves conditioning but the inferred significance remains covariance-estimator dependent: -1.779 sigma with OAS versus -0.722 sigma with the raw-sample/Hartlap control. The Abacus result is therefore used to validate physical mock covariance, survey-window response and injection recovery, not to replace the pre-existing primary real-data DESI fit.

interpretation: PASS_NULL. All 25 Abacus realizations completed. The OAS-calibrated conservative real-data coefficient is a sub-2-sigma negative fluctuation with empirical two-sided p=0.0769; the Hartlap sample-covariance control is only 0.72 sigma. No detection is claimed. Unit injections are recovered without measurable bias. This layer is a high-fidelity validation cross-check, not the publication headline likelihood.
guardrail: The amplitude is calibrated to the predeclared luminosity-rank proxy pair model. A physical halo-mass wake amplitude requires a separate proxy-to-halo calibration. The finite 25-mock covariance ensemble prevents this cross-check from superseding the primary full-sample DESI inference.
